newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market at standstill - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market at standstill - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained at a standstill near midday Monday, with no sales or bids reported, feedlot sources said.
Cattle were priced at $73.00 to $74.00 per cwt and packer bids were expected at $72.00, unchanged from last week's top prices in the central and southern Plains, sources said.
At least four major beef packing plants were closed in observance of Monday's U.S. Veterans Day holiday.
IBP last week said its plants at Amarillo, Texas; Emporia, Kan.; and West Point, Neb. would be closed. National Beef Packing also said its Liberal, Kan., plant would be closed.

Prices were expected to be supported this week by continued tight supplies of choice cattle as owners keep selling cattle ahead of schedule to meet packer demand. Those cattle have largely been grading select, as they lack the number of days on feed to grade choice, sources noted.
This week's showlists were expected to contain a large number of cattle on feed 100 days or less.
Cattle prices also could be buoyed by expectations for strong beef demand and higher CME live cattle futures, market sources said.
